entries.title: Psalms 141:1
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
1 David prays that his suit may be acceptable; 3 his conscience sincere; 7 and his life free from snares.

A.M. 2946. B.C. 1058. make haste. 40:13; 69:17,18; 70:5; 71:12; 143:7; Job 7:21

entries.title: Psalms 141:2
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
Let my prayer.David, who was now driven from Judea, and far from the sanctuary, here prays that the devotion of his heart, and the elevation of his hands, might be accepted; that the one might ascend to heaven fragrant and well pleasing as the cloud of incense, and the other, in conjunction with it, be prevalent as the {minchah,} or evening oblation.

Pr 15:8 set forth. Heb. directed. 5:3 as incense. Ex 30:7-9,34-38; Le 10:1,2; 16:11-13; Nu 16:35,46-48; Mal 1:11 Lu 1:9,10; Re 5:8; 8:3,4 the lifting. 28:2; 63:4; 134:2; 1Ti 2:8 the evening. Ex 29:39,42; 1Ki 18:36; Ezr 9:4; Da 9:21; Ac 3:1

entries.title: Psalms 141:5
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: the righteous. 1Sa 25:31-34; 2Sa 12:7-13; 2Ch 16:7-10; 25:16; Pr 6:23; 9:8,9 Pr 15:5,22; 19:25; 25:12; 27:5,6; Ga 2:11-14; 6:1; Re 3:19 smite, etc. or, smite me kindly and reprove me; let nottheir precious oil break my head, etc. for yet my. 51:18; 125:4; Mt 5:44; 2Ti 1:16-18; Jas 5:14-16

entries.title: Psalms 141:8
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: mine eyes. 25:15; 123:1,2; 2Ch 20:12 leave not my soul destitute. Heb. make not my soul bare. 25:16,17; 102:17; 143:3,4; Isa 41:17; Joh 14:18
